newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly on riot news.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly on riot news.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was jolted briefly against the dollar in early trading on Friday following riots in the west Java town of Tasikmalaya, dealers said.
They said Singapore operators were seen trying to push the dollar up but met resistance from local operators.
"Singapore operators made spot reaction at the opening but were countered by local players. Offshore players seemed to feel strong local resistance and cut losses," one dealer said.
The dealer, for a U.S. bank, said spot rupiah fell briefly to 2,364.5 before recovering to around the opening level.
One local bank dealer said some local and state banks were seen capping the dollar from any upturn.
He said reaction was brief only because the riots were confined to Tasikmalaya and had not spread.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,363.0/63.5 at 0250 GMT against an opening of 2,362.0/63.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,362.5/63.0 and 2,362.25/62.50, respectively.
Dealers said ample rupiah supply in the money market also aided some weakening of the local currency.
However, the local bank dealer said overall sentiment on the rupiah remained firm despite excess supply.
"I think players are still speculating for a band widening. They remember previous central bank moves at year-end," he said.
Residents of Tasikmalaya said a crowd of several thousand people ran amok apparently after police had beaten a religious school teacher and his two students on Thursday.
They said the mob set fire to churches, shops, commercial buildings and vehicles. Tasikmalaya was quiet but tense on Friday morning, with the military reporting at least two dead.
Witnesses said the rioters had targeted ethnic Chinese businesses, and also burned down at least two Christian churches in the town of some 500,000 people.
Dealers said year-end factor seemed to have helped prevent a more drastic reaction in the foreign exchange market.
"People do not want to take up fresh positions at year-end. They mainly stayed squared despite the news," one said.
The foreign exchange market will be closed on December 31 and January 1. It will reopen on January 2.
The dealer said swap rates remained soft on ample rupiah supply. Overnight swap due Monday was at 0.2/0.3.
Tom/next swap was quoted at 0.53/0.56 points.
One-month swaps was at 13.70/14.40, two at 28.00/29.00, three at 41.5/42.5 and six at 84.50/86.50 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,358/2,550 and the conversion rate to 2,358/2,406 on Thursday.
